subject: english-language
title: Reading Across Texts
welcome_lead: Compare two texts and the patterns leap out.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on comparing texts across genres.
final_note: You can now compare texts by audience, purpose and form.

walkthroughs.body_html: Form = shape (article, poem, novel). Genre = type within a form (fantasy novel, opinion article).
A scientific article uses formal register and neutral tone. A blog might use informal register and friendly tone.
Headlines, columns, images and bullet points all signal text type. Use layout before you've read a word.

mcqs.q: What does Labov's research show about language variation?
options: Labov showed that working-class people speak ungrammatically.
Language varies systematically by social class, gender, age and context — and speakers shift style depending on formality, often unconsciously.

Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.
Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
